One square for each chapter of the books that name Matthew: 8 verses in 7 chapters. The darker the square, the more verses in it name him. Choose a chapter to read what happens there.
¶ And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.
The feast with publicans and sinners
No verse in John names him.
¶ And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
A publican, a collector of taxes and tolls. He was “sitting at the receipt of custom” when Jesus called him, and Matthew's own list calls him “Matthew the publican”.
Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Alphaeus
And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
Mark tells the call straight after Jesus came back to Capernaum and went out “by the sea side”, so the tax office stood at or near Capernaum by the order of events. No verse names his home town.

CHAPTER III · THE CHURCH IN ACTS

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
He is named with the other apostles in the upper room in Jerusalem after the ascension.
Peter, Andrew, James son of Zebedee, John son of Zebedee, Philip, Bartholomew and 5 more

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
The last verse that names him is Acts 1:13. After that Acts speaks of “the eleven” and “the twelve” as a body (Acts 2:14; 6:2) but never names him again.
Tradition, by who said it and when · 5 sources
What Scripture says of his end
Scripture's last mention of Matthew is Acts 1:13. It says nothing of where he went or how he died.

Are Matthew and Levi the same man? (Most widely held view first.)
Easton (1897); G. H. Schodde, ISBE (1915): “practically beyond all doubt”
The three call stories agree in setting, words and sequence, and Mark's and Luke's lists of the Twelve include a Matthew but no Levi.
